column1: # appimage catalog — apps installable via `appimage install -i` or `appimage install <name>`.
# Tab-separated columns:  name <TAB> source_url <TAB> guard <TAB> description
#                         [<TAB> flags]
#   - guard: name of an appimage-guards/<guard>.sh hook, or "-" for none
#   - flags: optional 5th column, comma-separated. Last on purpose, so the rows
#     without it keep parsing exactly as before. Understood values:
#       cli         the app is a CLI as well as a GUI, so the wrapper runs it in
#                   the foreground with output on the terminal when given
#                   arguments and detaches only when launched bare
#       inner-cli   the app bundles its own CLI at usr/bin/bin/<name> inside the
#                   image while the image's entrypoint is the GUI, which ignores
#                   CLI flags (VS Code and its forks). The wrapper keeps the
#                   image mounted and runs the bundled CLI instead. Detected
#                   automatically on install and on `appimage wrap`, so this is
#                   only ever needed to force it
#       no-sandbox  replay the sandbox switches from the app's own .desktop in
#                   the wrapper. Only for apps that will not start otherwise —
#                   it turns Chromium's sandbox off. Plenty of the Electron
#                   AppImages here ship --no-sandbox and run fine sandboxed
#                   anyway, so this is never applied automatically.
#   - source_url is a GitHub repo/release URL (preferred, enables updates), a
#     templated download URL, a "latest" URL marked with a trailing #latest, a
#     download page that links the current build marked with a trailing #page, or
#     a direct .AppImage URL (the last of these gets no updates)
#   - lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored
# Templated source_url: for projects that tag releases on GitHub but host the
# AppImage themselves, write the download URL with placeholders and append
# "#github=OWNER/REPO" to say where the version comes from. Placeholders:
# {tag} (v5.0.0), {version} (5.0.0), {arch} (x86_64/aarch64), {arch_short}
# (x64/arm64). Never pin a version here — it re-resolves on every update.
# Keep columns tab-separated (not spaces). Every field must be non-empty (use
# "-" for no guard) — adjacent tabs collapse when parsed and would misalign.
# code — the AppImage is back, with the `inner-cli` flag. Two things made it look
# worse than the .deb, and both are the same bug: the image's entrypoint is the
# GUI binary, so every CLI flag (--version, --install-extension, --remote) was
# answered with an empty window, and AppRun's PATH export leaked $APPDIR/usr/bin
# — where that GUI binary is *named* `code` — into every integrated terminal,
# where it shadowed ~/bin/code and went stale on each restart. `inner-cli` runs
# the CLI bundled at usr/bin/bin/code off a shared mount instead, which is what
# a .deb's /usr/share/code/bin/code does, and never goes through AppRun; the
# shell rc also strips any /tmp/.mount_* that an AppRun-launched app leaked.
# The flag is spelled out here for the record — appimage.sh detects a bundled CLI
# by itself now, so a VS Code fork installed from a bare URL gets the same
# treatment without having to be catalogued first.
# The .deb is still installable side by side: scripts/install/install-code-deb.sh.
code
column4: VS Code (official build, repackaged as an AppImage). The image's entrypoint is the GUI binary, which ignores CLI flags and opens an empty window instead, so this one needs inner-cli to reach the real CLI inside the image.

column4: Claude Desktop (community Linux build; personal hosts only)

column1: lmstudio
column4: LM Studio (local LLM runner; personal hosts only). Not on GitHub, so the version comes from where the vendor's "latest" URL redirects — the old entry pinned .../0.4.19-2/LM-Studio-0.4.19-2-x64.AppImage and could never update.

column1: discord
column4: Discord (unofficial community build by pkgforge-dev; personal hosts only)

column1: croc-gui
column4: Croc GUI (desktop front-end for the croc CLI; named croc-gui so it does not collide with the croc CLI from mise)

column1: t3-code
column4: T3 Code (t3.codes — desktop control plane for driving Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode et al from one window; the repo also cuts nightly prereleases, but /releases/latest keeps us on stable)

column1: sonic-pi
column4: Sonic Pi (live-coding music environment; self-hosted download, version tracked from GitHub releases)

column1: opencode-desktop
column4: OpenCode Desktop (GUI for the opencode agent; named opencode-desktop so it does not shadow the opencode CLI installed from mise as npm:opencode-ai — ~/bin sorts ahead of the mise shims)

column1: paseo
column4: Paseo (orchestrator for Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode across desktop, mobile and web). Ships one binary that is both the Electron app and the `paseo ls|run|status|logs` CLI, hence the cli flag. Its own .desktop is "Exec=AppRun --no-sandbox %U" — Electron 41 / Chrome 146 cannot start the namespace sandbox here and the setuid fallback can never work from a squashfs AppImage, so without that flag it dies on a /dev/shm error before painting a window.

column1: lossless-cut
column4: LosslessCut (lossless trimming/cutting of video and audio files, ffmpeg front-end)

column1: kdenlive
column4: Kdenlive (full non-linear video editor from KDE: multitrack timeline, effects, titles, proxy editing). KDE hosts the AppImage under a major.minor directory and its GitHub mirror has no releases, so the version comes from the link on the official download page.

column1: shotcut
column4: Shotcut (open-source video editor on MLT; lighter and quicker to learn than Kdenlive)

column1: pinta
column4: Pinta (simple Paint.NET-style image editor on GTK4/libadwaita: crop, rotate, resize, adjustments/effects, text, layers). Upstream ships no AppImage, only Flathub, so this is the unofficial pkgforge-dev build.
